newsitem.title: CANADA: Locked out Inco union to meet conciliator.
newsitem.headline: Locked out Inco union to meet conciliator.

text.p: The union locked out of Inco Ltd's facility in Manitoba said on Monday it will meet with a provincial government conciliator on Tuesday.
About 1,400 union workers were locked out of the plant on Sunday night after they voted 71 percent against Inco's final contract offer.
Talks broke down early Monday morning over wages and working hours. No further talks were planned.
The union will meet with the conciliator on Tuesday morning to brief the government appointee on the labor dispute, said union spokesman Nelson Pruder.
But the union is not obligated to continue working through the conciliator, said Pruder, speaking on behalf of United Steelworkers of America local 6166.
Inco produces about 100 million pounds of nickel a year from the Thompson area in northern Manitoba.
Inco has said it will keep its customers supplied during the lockout by using output from other Inco operations and by buying nickel on the open market.
Analysts have said they don't know how much nickel the company has in inventories at Thompson.
"They would have a hard time getting it out," said Pruder.

While picketing workers have been told not to physically prevent the company from shipping its product, provincial laws allow other unionized workers to refuse to handle material produced in a company locking out its workers, Pruder said.
The last time the Thompson plant shut down for a labor dispute was in 1981 when a strike closed the plant about four months, Pruder said.
